note: Controlled benchmark of the engine at commit fe2959d (v0.8.0 plus swiss-grid, testimonial-wall, schedule and category fixes, a deeper two-tone secondary accent, and gate checks for invisible text and empty grid holes). Haiku 5.5 without vs with the MCP, identical SPEC.md, same 60-call budget, four never-seen domains (foxglove florist, kestrel credit union, cadenza music academy, podhaven podcast hosting), engine frozen for the run. RESULT: engine 0/8, judged more template-like in 8/8; a regression from v0.8.0 (2/8) and the worst since v0.5.1. Judges' recurring words for the engine pages: centred hero plus browser-frame mockup, beige and green palette, card grids, weak spacing and empty gaps (a hero card with a dead empty lower strip), abstract or blob feature illustrations; for the baselines: bolder serif headline, richer and more specific palette per brief (plum and apricot for the florist, green and amber for the credit union), a specific hero object (practice card with staff and keys, balance and loan cards, an episode dashboard). The agents again chose the older field-notes or editorial-paper styles by patch, so the new styles were barely exercised. The spec forbids external images for both arms, so the photo, logo-prompt and placeholder tools were not exercised. COST: engine arm tokens 105k-129k vs baseline 103k-120k, tool calls 18-40 vs 15-26. DEFECTS named by agents (to fix): features[].art given as an object was silently ignored (only a plain SVG string worked); the florist category fell through to the SaaS template; the engine tints alternate feature cards in a different hue (the new two-tone layer) which an agent read as inconsistent; a hero schedule visual rendered empty on a first attempt. CONFOUNDS: several agents deleted their own scratch files. NOT deployed to Vercel (no VERCEL_TOKEN in this environment).
